operational-example.copy: Use Route Summary for one visible route option or active ETA banner before map routing, station detail, and route orchestration move into patterns.

scenario.title: Route ETA on map
scenario.meta: Destination, distance, ETA, and local action
rationale: The ZIP Rutas template shows this as an active route ETA banner over a map.
Flow keeps the component to one route option with destination, distance, ETA, and a local action.
Map tiles, selected station sheets, filters, routing state, and route calculation stay in patterns or templates.

items.rule: Frames a single route option with stable responsive width.
Names the route decision in plain operational language.
Expose ETA, distance, fuel, tolls, or policy status as text.
Provide route start or compare only when the user can act.
Marks warning or error routes without replacing the route name.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, warning, selected, focus, hover, default
items: Use article or group semantics for one route option.
Expose route metrics as text, not only icons.
Keep action buttons named and keyboard reachable.
Use warning copy for policy or route risks.
Keep focus visible on both card and actions.

variants.copy: Route Summary variants separate the active ETA banner from metric cards: compact mirrors the Rutas template banner, standard exposes one route option, compare supports adjacent route units, and policy marks route risk.

states.copy: Route Summary states show selection, attention, focus, hover, error, and disabled behavior without hiding route metrics.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the route summary job; state defines route availability or attention with the same metric structure.

full-width.copy: Route Summary can fill drawers, cards, and route panels while metrics keep readable wrapping.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use one route summary per row on phones and let metric groups wrap before reducing text size.

viewport-organization.copy: Route Summary should stay readable before maps and route patterns decide sequencing or comparison.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Stack metrics and preserve primary action access.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use alongside map previews when both remain legible.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Compare summaries in patterns, not inside the component.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify route title, ETA, variant, state, metric wrapping, and action clarity.

api-foundations.copy: Route Summary API exposes route identity, metrics, variant, state, and actions while Design System owns metric rhythm and accessibility.

props.name: state
props.type: default | hover | focus | selected | warning | disabled

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Disables route actions and communicates unavailable state.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Lets the route summary fill a parent route panel.

props.name: icon
props.notes: Leading route icon, usually navigation for the active ETA banner.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not hide route metrics behind icons.
Do not turn route comparison into a single component.
Do not remove actions without explaining the state.

rejectIf: Comparison logic lives inside the component.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Route Summary as one route option. Agents may place it when route metrics are known, but humans confirm decision impact, policy risk, and pattern composition.
canDecide: Use Route Summary for one route option.
Use compact when the route appears inside a constrained panel.
Use warning when policy or availability changes the decision.
mustAsk: The route affects money, safety, or compliance.
Multiple route options need ranking or filtering.
Metrics source or freshness is unclear.
rejectIf: The route has no visible title.
Route comparison is hidden inside the component.
miel.handoff: I am using Route Summary for one route option. Please confirm metric source, action behavior, policy risk, and whether route comparison belongs in a pattern.
